name: Mettler-Toledo
description: Mettler-Toledo makes precision weighing and measuring instruments: lab balances and pipettes, industrial scales, product-inspection systems and supermarket scales, and says it holds the number-one global position in most of its businesses. It earns money from selling the instrument, then from a large service business (service contracts, calibration, on-demand repairs and parts) that was about 25% of 2025 sales and $1,018.6 million, plus consumables. Customers are labs, factories and food retailers across more than 140 countries. The profit statement is reported by geography, not product, so profit by product line is not disclosed. It pays no dividend and spends cash on buybacks instead: $800 million in 2025.

employees.note: Total workforce about 18,100 including 1,500 temporary personnel; about 6,200 in Europe, 5,200 in the Americas, 6,700 in Asia and other; 9,300 in sales and service.

businessLines.name: Laboratory instruments and related service
businessLines.how: Sells precision lab balances, pipettes, titrators, pH meters, process analytics, thermal analysis and automated reactors to pharma, biotech, academic and chemical labs; instruments up front, then service contracts, calibration and consumables (pipette tips) over the installed base.

businessLines.name: Industrial instruments and related service (incl. product inspection)
businessLines.how: Sells industrial weighing instruments and terminals, metal detection, x-ray and checkweighing inspection systems, and track-and-trace/logistics scanning to factories, food processors, pharma packagers and transport firms; equipment sale then service and software.

businessLines.name: Food retailing products and services
businessLines.how: Sells weighing, labeling and fresh-goods software solutions to supermarkets and food retailers (counter, self-service, checkout scales), one-time hardware plus software and service.

brands.name: LabX (lab software), FreeWeigh.Net, FormWeigh.Net
brands.note: Software lines sold alongside instruments; revenue not broken out.
